title: The butterfly effect
summary: Run two double pendulums a millionth of a degree apart, watch them part, and measure the chaos.

steps.title: Two pendulums, one tiny difference
steps.text:
Hang a second rod and bob from the first and you get a double pendulum, one of the simplest chaotic systems.

This setup starts two of them: the solid one, and a faint twin whose lower rod starts just one millionth of a degree higher. Press Run and watch the Animation. For a while you cannot tell them apart.

check.hint: Load the setup, then press Run.
check.success: Watch until the faint twin goes its own way.

steps.title: How fast do they part?
steps.text:
Open the Divergence tab. The top plot shows the distance between the two pendulums on a logarithmic scale. It climbs along a straight line, which means the gap grows exponentially, until the twins are completely different.

The Summary tab gives the divergence time: when the lower bobs are 10 % of the pendulum's length apart.

check.success: A difference of 10⁻⁶ degrees becomes a completely different motion within seconds.

steps.title: Small swings are not chaotic
steps.text:
Chaos needs energy. Start both rods at 5° instead (Initial angle and Lower initial angle) and run again.

This time the twins stay together for the whole run: small swings are predictable.

check.success: No divergence: the twins swing together.

steps.title: Two ways to swing
steps.text: Small swings of a double pendulum are a mix of two normal modes: both rods swinging together (in phase), or against each other (anti-phase). Open the Analyze ▸ Modes tab to see them. With equal rods and bobs, the in-phase mode is the slower one.

check.hint: Run the 5° setup, then open the Analyze ▸ Modes tab.
check.success: About 2.62 s; the anti-phase mode takes about 1.09 s.

steps.title: Measure the chaos
steps.text:
The Lyapunov exponent λ measures how fast nearby starts separate: the gap grows like e^(λt). Above zero means chaos.

This setup starts from a large swing and ticks "Estimate the Lyapunov exponent". Run it and read λ on the Divergence tab or in the Summary.

check.success: λ is about 1 per second: the gap grows about e-fold every second.

steps.title: Order and chaos side by side
steps.text:
A Poincaré section records the lower rod each time the upper rod swings forward through the vertical. Regular motion leaves a few points or neat curves; chaos sprays them everywhere.

The Sweep tab is set up to vary the starting angle from 10° to 150°. Press Run sweep, then choose "Poincaré ω₂ (all values)" in the Plot list.
